blocks.s: 5. The soul, then, seeing that of itself it cannot reach the longed-for sweetness of knowledge and experience, and that the more it draws near to the deep heart the more God is exalted (Psalm 63:7-8), humbles itself and takes refuge in prayer, saying: Lord, who are not seen except by the clean of heart, I have searched by reading, I have sought by meditating, how true cleanness of heart may be had, so that by its means I might know you, at least in some small part. I sought thy face, O Lord, thy face I sought after (Psalm 26:8). Long have I meditated in my heart, and in my meditation a fire burned up, and the desire of knowing you more fully (Psalm 38:4). While you break the bread of holy Scripture for me, in the breaking of the bread there is great knowledge (Luke 24:30-31); and the more I know you, the more I desire to know you, no longer in the husk of the letter but in the sense of experience. And I do not ask this, Lord, for my merits, but for your mercy. For I confess that I am unworthy and a sinner; but even the little dogs eat of the crumbs that fall from the table of their masters (Matthew 15:27). Give me, Lord, the pledge of the inheritance to come, at least one drop of the heavenly rain, with which I may cool my thirst; for I burn with love.
